title.narrative: NIVA and ASF Collaboration Against Plastic Pollution in Mumbai (NILA)

description.narrative:
Marine litter, particularly plastic, poses serious environmental threats: large items damage habitats, while wildlife suffers from entanglement or ingestion. As plastics degrade, they fragment into microplastics, which are easily ingested or inhaled by organisms and humans, accumulating in tissues and carrying toxic chemicals potentially linked to severe health effects. Mumbai, the capital of Maharashtra and India’s financial hub, is a densely populated city grappling with economic inequality, poor air quality, urban flooding and generally poor environmental quality. Public beaches are also heavily littered posing hazards to communities and marine life.
The projects objective is to provide scientific support to map, systematize, and monitor macroplastic pollution at Versova Beach, while also contributing to awareness-raising activities. The overarching goal is to support the development of effective strategies for reducing marine litter in Mumbai.
The NILA project has three interlinked project outcomes: Outcome 1: Improved performance to map and assess plastic pollution at Versova beach, Mumbai; Outcome 2: Improved institutional capacity of Afroz Shah Foundation; Outcome 3: Improved understanding of beach litter sources and awareness about plastic pollution. These outcomes are interlinked and contribute to the overall impact of Reduction of marine litter and increased awareness of plastic pollution in Mumbai.
The project will, overall enhance technical knowledge, and capacity to carry out beach litter monitoring independently by the Indian side, while also providing novel data sets and increasing awareness. Technical advise, exchange of data sets and methodologies, educational workshops, and field visits of experts from Norway to India will form of the deliverables.
